Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: National Bank of Rwanda (NBR) has direct operational role: it operates RIPPS (Rwanda Integrated Payments Processing System) and is regulator/overseer/catalyst in RNPS, and the payment-system law assigns NBR responsibility to regulate/oversee/supervise payment systems and to "operate a clearing and settlement system."
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law N° 61 of 2021 governing the Payment System gives the National Bank of Rwanda (NBR) express statutory power to establish, own and operate clearing, settlement and securities settlement systems, and assigns it responsibility to operate a clearing and settlement system directly. This is corroborated by the AfricaNenda SIIPS 2023 case study on Rwanda's eKash instant payment system, which identifies NBR as the settlement agent that settles transactions via RIPPS (Rwanda Integrated Payments Processing System), Rwanda's RTGS, once daily, and by NBR's own payment systems webpage. The evidence supports 'Direct Operation', the top of this variable's 1-5 scale, so this row is escalated to human review per the top-of-scale protocol even though the score is unchanged.
revised_comments: The National Bank of Rwanda (NBR) holds direct operational responsibility for core national payment infrastructure, going beyond a purely regulatory role. Law N° 61 of 2021 governing the Payment System empowers NBR to establish, own and operate clearing, settlement and securities settlement systems. NBR directly operates the Rwanda Integrated Payments Processing System (RIPPS), Rwanda's real-time gross settlement system, and acts as settlement agent for eKash, the RSwitch-operated national instant payment scheme, settling positions between participants once daily via RIPPS.

Definition: Whether legal or regulatory requirements obligate payment service providers to notify users, regulators, and/or data protection authorities about payment data breaches, cybersecurity incidents, or unauthorized access within specified timeframes.
Comments: Rwanda’s Data Protection and Privacy Law provides mandatory breach notification (DPO/NCSA provides a ‘Report a Data Breach’ service; secondary summaries describe 48-hour notification obligations under the law).
revision_notes: Confirmed. Law N° 058/2021 of 13 October 2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy, Articles 43-45, imposes a mandatory breach notification regime: a data processor must notify the data controller within 48 hours of becoming aware of a breach, the controller must notify the supervisory authority (the Data Protection and Privacy Office, under the National Cyber Security Authority) within 48 hours, and a full written report is due within 72 hours; breaches likely to pose a high risk to data subjects must also be communicated to those affected. This applies to payment service providers acting as data controllers or processors. The evidence supports 'Mandatory', the top of this variable's 0-3 scale, so this row is escalated to human review per the top-of-scale protocol even though the score is unchanged.
revised_comments: Rwanda's Law N° 058/2021 of 13 October 2021 relating to the protection of personal data and privacy imposes a mandatory personal data breach notification requirement that covers payment service providers as data controllers and processors. Article 43 requires a data processor to notify the data controller within 48 hours of becoming aware of a breach, and requires the data controller to notify the Data Protection and Privacy Office within the same 48-hour window. Article 44 requires a full written report to the supervisory authority within 72 hours, and Article 45 requires notification to affected data subjects where the breach is likely to pose a high risk to their rights and freedoms. The Data Protection and Privacy Office operates a dedicated online "Report a Data Breach" service to receive these notifications.

Definition: Whether payment system operators or regulators regularly publish performance metrics and statistics on system usage, transaction volumes/values, participant numbers, uptime, and other operational indicators.
Comments: NBR provides public payment-system statistics (dedicated ‘Payment System Statistics’ page) and the payment-system law assigns NBR responsibility to “collect, compile and disseminate” payment-system statistics, but this step did not confirm quarterly/monthly publication cadence.
revision_notes: Score raised from 2 (Ad Hoc) to 3 (Annual). NBR publishes a Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement (MPFSS) on a fixed, recurring schedule twice a year, in March and September, confirmed across multiple editions from 2021 to 2025 on NBR's publications page and corroborated by New Times coverage of the September 2024 release. Each MPFSS includes a payment-systems section with transaction volumes, values and year-on-year growth for RIPPS, mobile payments, mobile banking and card channels. NBR also maintains a dedicated public payment statistics resource (covering cards, mobile payment and online transaction data) referenced on its Statistics page, though its precise update cadence could not be confirmed as the page is JavaScript-rendered and could not be crawled directly. This is a scheduled, regular disclosure rather than ad hoc, but the confirmed semi-annual cadence sits between the scale's 'Annual' and 'Monthly/Quarterly' bands, so the score is recalculated to 3 (Annual) as the more defensible fit and this row is flagged for human review to confirm the closest-fit category.
revised_comments: The National Bank of Rwanda publishes payment-system performance data on a scheduled, recurring basis through its Monetary Policy and Financial Stability Statement, released twice yearly each March and September, which reports transaction volumes, values and year-on-year growth for RIPPS, mobile payments, mobile banking and card channels. NBR also maintains a dedicated public payment statistics page covering cards, mobile payment and online transaction data.
